newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower as funds carry session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower as funds carry session.

text.p: COMEX copper closed sharply lower at a six-and-a-half month low, sustaining another fund selling spree leading some brokers predict prices moving to as low as 83 cents a pound.
London led most of the action Monday, holding support at $2,135 a tonne, but commission house brokers warned that the next level of support was $2,085 a tonne, followed by $1,835 a tonne.

The COMEX December contract settled at 96.95 cents a lb, down 2.80 cents from Friday. September closed at 96.70 cents a lb, down 3.30 cents. The spot month settled at 96.50 cents a lb, down 2.90 cents.

"The (London) contangos came in pretty steep, which indicated some heavy lending which looked like it came from the Far East," one broker said. "Producers were starting eye put (options) below the market, which is not a very good sign."
The LME cash-to-three-month spread was a $6/$2 contango, up from a $3 Friday. The COMEX Sept-Dec spread closed at a 0.25-cent contango from a 1.20-cent back Friday.

In New York, funds carried the day, although the market was divided over whether the selling was liquidation or fresh selling. "It felt more like liquidation to me," the broker said. "We had some fresh selling Friday underneath 102.80 (in September). But today looked like the longs getting out."
Floor brokers said earlier in the session that the selling looked fresh.

Arbitrage dealers were scale-down buyers throughout the session. "COMEX (spot) had been trading at a premium to the LME (cash), but when the market flipped into an LME premium, the arb short covered and took some profits," one source said.
The LME cash price at the evening evaulation was at a 1.38 cent premium to the COMEX spot price.

Further arbitrage dealings are seen on the horizon as copper continues to flow into COMEX and LME warehouses in Baltimore, dealers said. In the last three trading days, Baltimore stocks have increased 4,592 tonnes.
Fundamentally, the market is still eyeing climbing LME stocks, up 3,725 tonnes to 264,600 tonnes in the latest report.

"There's also the feeling that copper is suffering at the hands of stock market," another trader said, noting that the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 247 points in Friday's market and is looking weaker Monday.
In other news, the strike at Falconbridge has moved into its third week, with negotiations centered around shift scheduling.
